title: Annual Plan, Budget & Endowments
summary: This capability lets the foundation define its annual plan as a budget ceiling broken down into tracks, items and initiatives, and follow in real time how much of each part of the plan is committed, due, paid, temporarily reserved and still available. Every change to the approved budget (increase, decrease, transfer, structural edit, plan closure) must be backed by an official document and leave an auditable trail. The capability also manages the endowments that fund the plan, recording their funding and the share each endowment carries of each plan item, so that management, finance and endowment boards can see exactly where the money comes from and where it goes.

process.title: Annual plan and budget lifecycle
process.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["Create annual plan"] --> B["Build tracks, items and initiatives"]
  B --> C["Save changes with official document"]
  C --> D["Approve and activate plan"]
  D --> E["Link opportunities, applications and projects to plan items"]
  E --> F["Monitor committed, due, paid and available amounts"]
  F --> G{"Budget change needed?"}
  G -->|"Yes"| H["Increase, decrease or transfer with evidence"]
  H --> F
  G -->|"No"| I["Lock plan at year end"]
  I --> J["Keep or carry over open obligations"]
  K["Record endowment funding"] --> L["Set endowment shares of plan items"]
  L --> F

use_cases.name: Browse the annual plans portfolio
use_cases.title: As a Grants Manager, I want to see all annual plans with their budget, spending and indicator achievement so that I can monitor the plan portfolio at a glance.
use_cases.description: Staff open the annual plans register to see every plan of their organization with its year, budget, spending progress, indicator achievement, active and approval status. Portfolio-level indicators summarise the number of plans, the share of approved budgets already paid out and the budget-weighted indicator achievement. From the register the user opens a plan, starts a budget operation, edits the plan or locks it.
preconditions: The user is signed in with a role allowed to view annual plans.
At least one annual plan exists for the user's organization (otherwise an empty list is shown).
use_cases.trigger: The user selects «الخطة السنوية» from the main menu or from global search.
scenario: The user opens the annual plans register.
The system shows the portfolio indicators: number of plans, spending from budget across approved plans, and budget-weighted indicator achievement.
The system lists the organization's plans, newest year first, with name, year, budget, spending progress, indicator achievement, active status and approval status.
The user filters the list by active status, approval status, year and creation date range.
The system remembers the user's preferred filters, visible columns and page size for the next visit.
The user optionally exports the visible list.
The user opens a plan's summary by clicking its row, or chooses an action from the row menu (increase, decrease, transfer, edit plan and approval, lock/reopen).
alternative_flows: If no plan matches the filters, the system shows an empty list and the user can clear the filters.
If the user selects a row action, the corresponding use case starts (PLN-3, PLN-5 or PLN-7).
business_requirements: The system must list only the annual plans of the user's own organization.
The system must show for each plan its name, year, budget, spending from budget (%), indicator achievement (%), active status and approval status.
The system must allow the plan reference number and creation date to be shown as optional columns.
The system must allow filtering by active status, approval status, year and creation date range.
The system should remember each user's filters, hidden columns and page size between visits.
The system must calculate portfolio spending as the total paid across approved plans divided by their total budget.
The system must calculate portfolio indicator achievement as the budget-weighted average of approved plans' achievement.
The system must allow exporting the plans list, excluding action buttons.
The system must show each plan's lock status with a distinct, clearly labelled icon.
The system must restrict access to the register and its actions according to the approved permission matrix (To be confirmed).

errors.name: Data not available
errors.description: If plan data cannot be loaded, the system shows an error state and asks the user to retry; no partial figures are shown.

use_cases.postconditions: The user has an up-to-date view of the plan portfolio and can navigate to any plan or plan action.

use_cases.name: Create an annual plan
use_cases.title: As a Grants Manager, I want to create a new annual plan with its name, year and budget so that next year's grants and initiatives can be planned against an approved ceiling.
use_cases.description: The Grants Manager creates a new annual plan by entering its name, year and total budget. The plan starts as active and not yet approved; its structure (tracks and items) is then built in the plan edit session. An AI assistant can propose the name, year and budget from a free-text description, but values are applied only when the user accepts them.
preconditions: The user is authorised to create annual plans (To be confirmed).
use_cases.trigger: The user selects «خطة جديدة» on the annual plans register.
scenario: The user selects «خطة جديدة».
The system opens the plan form prefilled with next year, active = yes and approved = no.
Optionally, the user describes the plan in free text and the AI Assistant proposes a name, year and budget.
The user reviews and applies or ignores the AI proposal.
The user enters or confirms the plan name, year and total budget.
The user selects «حفظ».
The system validates the data, creates the plan for the user's organization and assigns a plan reference number.
The system confirms «تم حفظ الخطة» and shows the plan in the register.
alternative_flows: If the user cancels, no plan is created.
If the AI proposal is not suitable, the user ignores it and enters the values manually.
business_requirements: The system must require a plan name and year.
The system must require a total budget that is a valid amount of zero or more.
The system must create new plans as active and not approved by default.
The system must assign each plan a unique reference number automatically.
The system must create the plan under the organization of the signed-in user.
The system should offer AI-assisted proposal of name, year and budget, applied only on user confirmation.
The system should warn when another plan already exists for the same year in the organization (To be confirmed).
The system must record who created the plan and when (Recommended).

errors.name: Missing name or year
errors.description: If the name or year is empty, the system shows «الاسم والسنة مطلوبان» and does not save.

errors.name: Invalid budget
errors.description: If the budget is missing or not a valid amount, the system shows «أدخل موازنة صحيحة» and does not save.

use_cases.postconditions: A new active, unapproved plan exists with a reference number and is ready for structure building.

fields.notes: Zero or more; thousands separators; Arabic digits accepted

use_cases.name: Build, restructure and approve a plan in an evidenced edit session
use_cases.title: As a Grants Manager, I want to add and change plan tracks, items and the plan header in one edit session and save them together with one official document so that every change to the approved plan is justified and auditable.
use_cases.description: Plan structure and header changes (name, year, budget, active and approval flags, level names and amounts, new tracks and sub-items) are drafted in an explicit edit mode. The system previews all figures and warnings with the draft applied, then commits all changes at once. Any change to an existing element requires an official document; each change is recorded in the plan's edit history with before and after values. Leaf items can carry performance indicators.
preconditions: The user is authorised to edit plan structure and approval (To be confirmed).
use_cases.trigger: The user selects «تعديل الخطة» on a plan view or «تعديل الخطة والاعتماد» on the register.
scenario: The system switches the plan to edit mode and shows the unsaved-changes banner.
The user adds a root track or a sub-level under any level, giving its name and allocated amount; the system assigns the hierarchical code automatically.
The user edits the name or amount of existing levels.
The user edits the plan header, including name, year, budget, active and approved flags.
The system recalculates all amounts, breakdowns and warnings with the draft applied, highlights changed items and shows the number of unsaved changes.
The system warns when the sum of a level's children differs from its amount.
The user defines indicators on leaf items where needed.
The user selects «حفظ التعديلات»; the system lists all pending changes.
The user attaches the official document when any existing element changed and selects «حفظ الكل».
The system saves all changes together, records each change in the edit history with the document and confirms «تم حفظ {n} تعديل».
alternative_flows: If the session contains only new levels, the system states «إضافات فقط — لا يلزم مستند نظامي.» (To be confirmed whether additions to an approved plan also need a document).
If the user selects «إلغاء», all draft changes are discarded and the plan returns to view mode.
If a level's value is edited back to its original value, the system drops that pending change.
If the user tries to leave the page with unsaved changes, the system warns before discarding them (Recommended).
business_requirements: The system must allow plan structure and header changes only inside an explicit edit session.
The system must generate hierarchical level codes automatically (e.g. 1, 1.2, 1.2.3).
The system must require a name and a valid amount of zero or more for each level.
The system must preview all figures and warnings with draft changes applied before saving.
The system must warn, without blocking, when children amounts do not add up to the parent amount, showing the difference (To be confirmed whether this should block approval).
The system must require one official document when any existing plan element is changed.
The system must save all changes of a session together or none of them; on failure nothing is changed and the uploaded document is discarded.
The system must record every change, including added levels, in the plan edit history with before and after values, the actor, date and document.
The system must allow cancelling a session, discarding all draft changes.
The system must allow approving or un-approving a plan only through an evidenced change by an authorised approver (To be confirmed).
The system must allow indicators only on leaf items and must not allow deleting an indicator that is linked to applications or projects.
The system should allow deleting or moving levels with safeguards for linked projects, applications and indicators (To be confirmed).

errors.name: Missing level name
errors.description: If a level has no name, the system shows «الاسم مطلوب».

errors.name: Invalid level amount
errors.description: If the amount is missing or invalid, the system shows «أدخل مبلغاً صحيحاً».

errors.name: Missing or invalid document
errors.description: If a required document is missing, of an unaccepted format or larger than 10 MB, the system blocks saving and explains the reason.

errors.name: Save failure
errors.description: If saving fails, the system shows «تعذر حفظ بعض التعديلات» and keeps the plan unchanged.

use_cases.postconditions: The plan reflects the saved structure and header, and the edit history shows each change with its supporting document.

fields.notes: Generated from parent code and position
Required when existing elements change; PDF, Word, Excel or image; max 10 MB; advisory AI check
Greater than zero; milestone target is 1

use_cases.name: Monitor plan budget performance
use_cases.title: As a Finance Officer, I want to see for the plan and each of its levels how much is committed, due, paid, temporarily reserved and still available so that I can control spending against the approved ceiling.
use_cases.description: Each plan offers three views built on the same budget figures: a one-page summary, a hierarchical view and a tree diagram. For the plan and every level the system shows the allocated amount split into paid, due, committed and available, with temporarily reserved amounts shown separately. Users can drill down to the projects and applications charged to a level and see initiatives, recent financial operations and edit history.
preconditions: The plan exists and the user is authorised to view it.
use_cases.trigger: The user opens a plan from the register or from a link in another screen.
scenario: The system opens the plan summary showing year, approval and active status, total budget and the plan-level breakdown (paid, due, committed, available, temporarily reserved).
The system shows spending from budget, spending of committed amounts and indicator achievement.
The system shows the breakdown per track and flags any track that exceeds its budget with «تجاوز الموازنة».
The system lists initiatives linked to the plan with their progress and budget, and the five latest financial operations.
The user switches to the hierarchical view to see each track and level with its amount, breakdown and warnings.
The user selects «المشاريع: n» or «الطلبات: n» on a level to list the projects or applications charged to it and its sub-levels, and opens any of them.
The user switches to the tree view to see the plan structure with each level's amount and share of its parent.
The user reviews the plan edit history and opens the supporting documents.
alternative_flows: If the plan does not exist, the system shows «الخطة غير موجودة».
If the plan has no tracks, the system shows «لا توجد مسارات في الخطة.»
If a project is funded by several initiatives, its amounts and payments are split across those levels in proportion to each allocation.
business_requirements: The system must calculate used, committed, due, paid, available and temporarily reserved amounts for the plan and every level, including all sub-levels.
The system must use one single definition of each budget figure across all screens and reports.
The system must split a project funded by several plan items across those items in proportion to the allocated amounts, including its payments.
The system must show temporarily reserved amounts separately; they must not reduce the available balance.
The system must highlight negative available balances and flag tracks that exceed their budget.
The system must show the number of projects and applications charged to each level and its sub-levels, with drill-down lists.
The system must provide summary, hierarchical and tree views of the plan.
The system must show each level's share of its parent amount in the tree view.
The system must derive plan indicator achievement from leaf indicator targets and accepted evidence (To be confirmed).
The system must flag projects whose payments exceed their budget (Recommended).

errors.name: Plan not found
errors.description: If the requested plan does not exist or is not accessible, the system shows «الخطة غير موجودة».

use_cases.postconditions: The user has an accurate picture of the plan's financial position and can navigate to underlying projects and applications.

use_cases.name: Adjust a plan budget (increase, decrease or transfer)
use_cases.title: As a Finance Officer, I want to increase, decrease or transfer budget between plan items with an official document so that the plan reflects approved budget decisions.
use_cases.description: Approved budget decisions are executed as financial operations on plan levels. An increase raises a level, its parent levels and the plan budget; a decrease lowers them within the level's actual available balance; a transfer moves an amount from one level to another without changing the plan total. Every operation requires an official document and is recorded with a reference number.
preconditions: The plan exists and is in a state that allows the chosen operation (To be confirmed).
The user is authorised to execute budget operations (To be confirmed).
use_cases.trigger: The user selects «تعزيز موازنة», «تخفيض موازنة» or «نقل المخصصات المالية» from the plan register menu or the financial operations page.
scenario: The user selects the operation type and the plan.
The system opens the operation form for that plan and type.
The user selects the target level (increase), the source level (decrease) or both source and target levels (transfer).
The system shows the selected level's amount and actual available balance.
The user enters the amount and an optional note and attaches the official document.
The system runs an advisory AI check on the document and shows its verdict.
The user selects «تنفيذ».
The system validates the operation, updates the level, its parent levels and (for increase/decrease) the plan budget in a single step.
The system records the operation with a reference number, the actor, date and document, and confirms «تم تنفيذ {type}».
alternative_flows: If the user opens the operation from the financial operations page without choosing a plan, the system asks the user to select the plan first.
If the operation is subject to approval, it is submitted to the approver and applied only after approval (To be confirmed).
business_requirements: The system must require an amount greater than zero.
The system must require an official document (PDF, Word, Excel or image, maximum 10 MB) for every operation.
The system must require a target level for an increase, a source level for a decrease, and different source and target levels for a transfer.
The system must not allow a decrease or transfer greater than the source level's actual available balance.
The system must validate decreases and transfers from a parent level against its unallocated balance, or cascade the change to a chosen child (To be confirmed).
The system must not allow transfers between a level and its own parent or child unless explicit rules are defined (To be confirmed).
The system must apply an increase or decrease to the level, all its parent levels and the plan budget.
The system must apply a transfer along both branches and keep the plan budget unchanged.
The system must apply each operation completely or not at all, and must prevent concurrent operations from overwriting each other.
The system must record each operation with a unique reference number, type, levels, amount, note, actor, date and document.
The system must enforce which operations are allowed on unapproved, inactive or locked plans (To be confirmed).
The system should support a maker-checker approval step before an operation is applied (To be confirmed).

errors.name: Invalid amount
errors.description: If the amount is zero or empty, the system shows «أدخل قيمة أكبر من صفر».

errors.name: Level not selected
errors.description: If a required level is missing, the system shows «اختر المستوى المراد تعزيزه», «اختر المستوى المصدر» or «اختر المستوى الهدف».

errors.name: Same level transfer
errors.description: If source and target are the same, the system shows «لا يمكن النقل إلى نفس المستوى».

errors.name: Exceeds available
errors.description: If the amount exceeds the source's actual available balance, the system shows «القيمة تتجاوز المتاح الفعلي للمستوى (…)».

errors.name: Invalid document
errors.description: If the document is missing, of an unaccepted format or larger than 10 MB, the system blocks the operation with an explanatory message.

use_cases.postconditions: Level and plan amounts reflect the operation, and the operation appears in the financial operations register with its document.

fields.notes: Transfer only; must differ from source
Greater than zero; not above actual available for decrease/transfer
PDF, Word, Excel or image; max 10 MB

use_cases.name: Review financial operations and plan change history
use_cases.title: As a Finance Officer, I want a register of all budget operations and plan edits with their supporting documents so that I can audit every change to the budget.
use_cases.description: The financial operations register lists all increases, decreases and transfers with their reference, plan, levels, amount, creator, note, document and date. Each plan also shows its edit history with the documents supporting structural changes. Auditors and finance staff use these records to trace every budget change to an official decision.
preconditions: The user is authorised to view financial operations.
use_cases.trigger: The user selects «العمليات المالية» on the plans register, or opens a plan's edit history.
scenario: The user opens the financial operations register.
The system shows tabs for increases, decreases and transfers.
The user filters the operations by plan.
The system lists reference number, plan, level(s), amount, creator, note, document and date for each operation.
The user opens the supporting document of an operation.
The user exports the current tab.
From any plan view, the user reviews the plan edit history (plan or level change, element name, date, document) and opens the documents.
alternative_flows: If the user starts a new operation from this page, use case PLN-5 starts for the plan selected in the filter.
business_requirements: The system must list all budget operations of the organization, grouped by type.
The system must allow filtering operations by plan.
The system must show decreases visually distinct from increases.
The system must allow authorised users to open supporting documents securely through time-limited access.
The system must allow exporting the operations list, excluding document links.
The system must show the plan edit history, newest first, on all plan views.
The system must keep the edit history and operations register append-only; records cannot be edited or deleted.
The system must record plan lock and reopen decisions in the plan history (Recommended).

errors.name: Document cannot be opened
errors.description: If the document cannot be retrieved, the system shows «تعذر فتح الشاهد النظامي».

use_cases.postconditions: The user has a complete, evidenced audit trail of budget operations and plan changes.

use_cases.name: Lock and reopen a plan budget
use_cases.title: As a Finance Officer, I want to lock a plan's budget with a documented decision so that no new projects are approved from a closed year, and to reopen it when authorised.
use_cases.description: At year end, or when management decides, a plan's budget is locked so that no new projects can be approved from it while running projects continue. Before locking, the user decides how open obligations are treated (kept on this plan or carried over to the next plan) and attaches the decision or minutes. A locked plan can be reopened by an authorised user.
preconditions: The user is authorised to lock or reopen plans (To be confirmed).
use_cases.trigger: The user selects the lock icon of a plan on the register.
scenario: The system asks for confirmation «إغلاق «{name}»؟ لن تُعتمد مشاريع جديدة من ميزانيتها.»
The user chooses the treatment of contracted obligations not yet due: continue on this plan or carry over to the next plan.
The user chooses the treatment of due obligations not yet paid: continue on this plan or carry over to the next plan.
The user attaches the decision or minutes.
The user selects «إغلاق الخطة».
The system locks the plan, stores the choices and document in the plan history, and applies the chosen carry-over treatment.
The system removes the plan's items from the lists used to link new applications, projects and opportunities.
The system confirms the lock, echoing the chosen treatments.
alternative_flows: Reopen: the user selects the lock icon of a locked plan, attaches the justification document (Recommended) and confirms «إعادة الفتح»; the plan accepts new approvals again.
If the user cancels, the plan remains unchanged.
business_requirements: The system must require a choice for each of the two obligation categories before locking.
The system must require a decision or minutes document to lock a plan.
The system must store the lock decision, choices, actor, date and document in the plan history.
The system must refuse to convert approved applications into projects charged to a locked plan.
The system must exclude items of locked or inactive plans from selection lists for new links, while keeping existing links visible.
The system must allow running projects of a locked plan to continue, including their payments.
The system must apply the carry-over treatment to obligations marked «ترحَّل للخطة القادمة» (To be confirmed).
The system must require a justification document and record the reopening of a locked plan (Recommended).
The system must restrict lock and reopen to authorised roles (To be confirmed).

errors.name: Incomplete lock data
errors.description: If either obligation choice or the document is missing, the system keeps the «إغلاق الخطة» button disabled.

errors.name: Approval from locked plan
errors.description: If a user tries to convert an application into a project on a locked plan item, the system shows «ميزانية «…» مقفلة — لا يمكن اعتماد مشاريع جديدة منها».

use_cases.postconditions: The plan is locked (or reopened), its decision is documented, and new approvals are blocked (or allowed) accordingly.

fields.notes: تستمر على هذه الخطة / ترحَّل للخطة القادمة
تستمر على هذه الخطة / ترحَّل للخطة القادمة

use_cases.name: Record endowment funding
use_cases.title: As a Finance Officer, I want to record each funding movement of an endowment with its official document so that the endowment's current size is known and traceable.
use_cases.description: Endowments are the funding sources of the plan. Each time an endowment is topped up, the Finance Officer records the amount, date and supporting document. The endowment's current size is the total of its recorded fundings and is used to distribute plan shares in proportion to endowment size.
preconditions: The endowment exists and is active (maintained in system settings).
The user is authorised to record fundings (To be confirmed).
use_cases.trigger: The user selects «تغذية الوقف» on the endowment page.
scenario: The user opens the endowment page from settings or from an endowment label on the plan.
The system shows the endowment's current size, its share of plan budgets, the amount used and the amount available.
The user selects «تغذية الوقف».
The user enters the amount, funding date (default today) and an optional note, and attaches the official document.
The system runs an advisory AI check on the document.
The user selects «حفظ».
The system records the funding and confirms «تم تسجيل التغذية».
The system updates the endowment size and the funding ledger.
alternative_flows: If a funding was recorded in error, an authorised user records an evidenced reversal entry (To be confirmed).
business_requirements: The system must require a funding amount greater than zero.
The system must require a funding date, defaulting to today.
The system must require an official document for each funding.
The system must calculate endowment size as the total of its recorded fundings.
The system must show the funding ledger with date, amount, note and a document that can be opened.
The system must not allow fundings to be edited or deleted; corrections must be made by an evidenced reversal entry (To be confirmed).
The system must record who recorded each funding and when.

errors.name: Invalid amount
errors.description: If the amount is missing or not positive, the system shows «أدخل مبلغاً صحيحاً».

errors.name: Missing document
errors.description: If no document is attached, the system shows «أرفق المستند النظامي».

errors.name: Invalid document
errors.description: If the document format is not accepted or it exceeds 10 MB, the system rejects it with an explanatory message.

use_cases.postconditions: The funding is recorded, the endowment size is updated and the document is retrievable.

fields.notes: PDF, Word, Excel or image; max 10 MB

use_cases.name: Manage endowment participation and review endowment share
use_cases.title: As a Grants Manager, I want to set which endowments fund each plan item and see each endowment's share, usage and funded projects so that funding sources are transparent to management and endowment boards.
use_cases.description: When the organization has two or more active endowments, each plan item is funded by a set of endowments with percentage shares. By default all endowments participate equally; a level can have its own split, otherwise it inherits its parent's split. The endowment page shows the endowment's share of each plan, how much of that share is used and available, and the projects it funds.
preconditions: The organization has at least two active endowments.
The user is authorised to change endowment participation (To be confirmed).
use_cases.trigger: The user opens an endowment page and reviews «المشاركة في عناصر الخطة».
scenario: The system lists every level of each plan with the endowment's percentage and the number of participating endowments.
The user switches the endowment's participation on or off for a level.
The system redistributes that level's shares equally among the participating endowments and ensures at least one endowment remains.
The user attaches the supporting document for the participation change (Recommended).
The system records the change in the plan history and confirms «تم تحديث المشاركة».
The system shows, per plan, the endowment's share, used and available amounts, and the levels it funds with inherited shares marked «(موروث)».
The system lists the projects funded by the endowment with budget, percentage, endowment share and status.
alternative_flows: If the organization has only one active endowment, it funds 100% of every level and the participation section is hidden.
If the endowment does not fund any track, the system shows «لا يتبنى هذا الوقف أي مسار بعد.»
business_requirements: The system must ensure endowment shares of each level total exactly 100%.
The system must ensure at least one endowment participates in every level.
The system must apply a level's own split, otherwise inherit the nearest parent's split, otherwise split equally among active endowments.
The system must support equal split and split proportional to endowment size.
The system must exclude inactive endowments from shares and re-distribute their portion, or prevent deactivation while shares exist.
The system must calculate an endowment's share of a plan from each level's unallocated amount multiplied by the endowment's percentage.
The system must calculate endowment used and available amounts from the projects and approved applications charged to its levels.
The system must show per-level figures that reconcile with the endowment's total share.
The system must require an official document and record a history entry for participation and split changes (To be confirmed).
The system must decide one place where endowment splits are maintained (plan edit session or endowment page) (To be confirmed).

errors.name: Shares not 100%
errors.description: If shares do not total 100%, the system shows «مجموع نسب الأوقاف يجب أن يساوي 100%».

errors.name: No participating endowment
errors.description: If the change would leave a level without an endowment, the system shows «يجب أن يشارك وقف واحد على الأقل في كل مستوى».

errors.name: Endowment not found
errors.description: If the endowment does not exist, the system shows «الوقف غير موجود».

use_cases.postconditions: Each plan level has a valid endowment split, and the endowment's share, usage and funded projects are visible.

use_cases.name: Link applications, projects and opportunities to plan items
use_cases.title: As a Grants Manager, I want every application, project and grant opportunity linked to a plan item or initiative so that spending is always charged to the right part of the plan.
use_cases.description: Grant opportunities carry a default plan item; applications and projects are linked to a plan item, and applicants on general opportunities choose the initiative their request serves. Only items of active, unlocked plans can be selected. Initiatives run by the foundation itself are managed as projects with activity-based progress.
preconditions: At least one active, unlocked plan with sub-levels exists.
use_cases.trigger: The user sets the plan item on an opportunity, application or project, or an applicant fills an application on a general opportunity.
scenario: The user opens the plan item selector on the opportunity, application or project.
The system lists the non-root items of active, unlocked plans, labelled with year, code and name.
The user selects an item or removes the link.
The system saves the link and immediately reflects the amounts in the plan figures.
On a general opportunity, the applicant selects «المبادرة» the request serves before submitting.
When an approved application is converted to a project, the system charges it to the selected plan item, or to the opportunity's default item.
Initiatives appear in the projects list and in the plan summary with progress calculated from weighted activities.
alternative_flows: If no active unlocked plan exists, the selector is empty and the user is informed.
If an existing link points to a locked or inactive plan, the link remains visible but cannot be newly selected.
business_requirements: The system must allow linking only to non-root items (items and initiatives) of active, unlocked plans.
The system must label items with plan year, code and name.
The system must require applicants on general opportunities to choose the initiative their request serves.
The system must charge applications on initiative-specific opportunities to the opportunity's default plan item.
The system must refuse to convert an approved application into a project charged to a locked plan.
The system must allow a project to be split across several plan items with allocated amounts.
The system must calculate initiative progress as the weighted average of its activities' progress, falling back to the recorded progress.
The system should decide whether unapproved plans can be used for linking (To be confirmed).

business_rules.rule: Used amount of a level = total budget of projects charged to the level or its sub-levels + requested amounts of approved applications not yet converted to projects.
Actual available of a level = allocated amount − used amount; it is the limit for decreases and transfers.
The allocated amount of a level is split into paid, due, committed (approved but not yet due) and available; available = allocated − committed − due − paid.
Temporarily reserved amounts (applications still under review) are shown for information only and never reduce the available balance.
A project funded by two or more plan items is counted at each item in proportion to its allocated amount, and its payments are split in the same proportion.
Cancelled payments are ignored; new (not yet due) payments remain within the committed amount.
Every budget increase, decrease or transfer requires an amount greater than zero and an official document.
An increase or decrease changes the level, all its parent levels and the plan budget by the same amount; a transfer leaves the plan budget unchanged.
A decrease or transfer cannot exceed the source level's actual available balance.
Plan structure and header changes, including approval and active status, are made only in an edit session and saved together with one official document when existing elements change.
Level codes are generated automatically from the parent code and the next sequence number.
A mismatch between the sum of child amounts and the parent amount produces a warning (blocking at approval to be confirmed).
Indicators are defined only on leaf plan items; an indicator linked to applications or projects cannot be deleted.
Edit history and financial operation records are append-only.
Locking a plan requires a decision for both obligation categories and a decision document; a locked plan accepts no new project approvals, while running projects continue.
Only non-root items of active, unlocked plans can be selected for new links.
Applicants on general opportunities must choose an initiative; applications on initiative-specific opportunities inherit the opportunity's default plan item.
Endowment size equals the total of its recorded fundings; each funding needs an amount greater than zero, a date and an official document.
Endowment shares of each level total exactly 100% and at least one endowment participates in every level.
A level uses its own endowment split, otherwise its nearest parent's split, otherwise an equal split among active endowments; with a single active endowment it carries 100%.
Equal split gives each endowment the same whole percentage, with any remainder given to the first endowment (e.g. 34/33/33); size-weighted split follows recorded endowment sizes.
An endowment's share of a plan counts each level's unallocated amount times the endowment's percentage, so amounts are not double counted across parent and child levels.
Initiatives are projects run by the foundation; their progress is the weighted average of their activities' progress.
Plans and budget operations receive unique reference numbers automatically (PLN-…, ADJ-…).

kpis.name: Total budget (الموازنة الإجمالية)
kpis.definition: The approved ceiling of the plan or of a plan item: the maximum amount the foundation has decided to spend on it this year, after all approved increases, decreases and transfers.

kpis.name: Used (المستخدم)
kpis.definition: The part of the budget already taken by funding decisions: the full budget of every project charged to the item plus the requested amount of every approved application not yet turned into a project. It includes amounts already paid, due or still committed.

kpis.name: Committed (المعتمد — متعاقد عليه غير مستحق)
kpis.definition: Money the foundation has promised but that is not yet payable: approved project budgets and approved applications, minus what has already become due or been paid.

kpis.name: Due (المستحق — مستحق غير مصروف)
kpis.definition: Payments that have become payable to partners (due, awaiting approval or awaiting transfer) but have not yet been transferred.

kpis.name: Paid (المصروف — تم التحويل)
kpis.definition: Money actually transferred to partners (paid or awaiting the partner's receipt confirmation).

kpis.name: Available (المتاح — الرصيد الحر)
kpis.definition: The free balance still open for new approvals: total budget minus committed, due and paid. A negative value means the item is over-committed and is shown in red.

kpis.name: Actual available for adjustments (المتاح الفعلي)
kpis.definition: The amount that can be safely reduced or transferred out of an item: its budget minus the used amount. Decreases and transfers cannot exceed it.

kpis.name: Pending / temporarily reserved (محجوز مؤقتاً)
kpis.definition: The requested amounts of applications still under review that are linked to the item. It is shown as an early warning of future demand and does not reduce the available balance (which review stages count is to be confirmed).

kpis.name: Spending from budget (الصرف من الموازنة)
kpis.definition: Paid amount divided by the total budget, as a percentage (capped at 100%). Shows how much of the year's ceiling has actually been disbursed.

kpis.name: Spending of committed (الصرف من المعتمد)
kpis.definition: Paid amount divided by everything approved (committed + due + paid), as a percentage. Shows how quickly approved grants are being paid out.

kpis.name: Portfolio spending (approved plans)
kpis.definition: Total paid across all approved plans divided by their total budget.

kpis.name: Indicator achievement (إنجاز المؤشرات)
kpis.definition: The plan's achievement against its performance indicators, as a percentage; at portfolio level it is weighted by each approved plan's budget (calculation method to be confirmed).

kpis.name: Number of plans (عدد الخطط)
kpis.definition: Count of annual plans of the organization.

kpis.name: Budget overrun flag (تجاوز الموازنة)
kpis.definition: Shown on any track whose available balance is below zero, i.e. commitments exceed the track's budget.

kpis.name: Endowment size (حجم الوقف الحالي)
kpis.definition: Total of all funding recorded for the endowment to date.

kpis.name: Endowment share of budgets (حصته من الموازنات)
kpis.definition: The part of plan budgets carried by the endowment according to its percentage in each plan item.

kpis.name: Endowment used / available (المستخدم / المتاح من حصته)
kpis.definition: The endowment's portion of the projects and approved applications it funds, and the remainder of its share still free for new approvals.

gaps.gap: Any signed-in user can create, edit, approve, adjust, lock and reopen plans and change endowment settings; restrictions exist only in the menu.
gaps.impact: Unauthorised budget changes and no segregation of duties.
gaps.recommendation: Define and enforce a permission matrix for every plan action, with maker-checker where required.

gaps.gap: A budget operation or plan edit session that fails part-way can leave amounts partly changed without a record.
gaps.impact: Plan figures may not reconcile with the operations register; audit trail is incomplete.
gaps.recommendation: Apply every operation and edit session completely or not at all, with server-side validation of availability.

gaps.gap: The lock decision document and the obligation choices are not stored, no history is written, carry-over is not applied and reopening needs no justification.
gaps.impact: Year-end closure decisions cannot be evidenced or audited.
gaps.recommendation: Store lock/reopen as evidenced, audited operations and implement carry-over behaviour.

gaps.gap: The temporarily reserved figure always shows zero because it does not match current application statuses.
gaps.impact: Management cannot see upcoming demand on plan items.
gaps.recommendation: Count applications under review linked to the item; confirm which stages count.

gaps.gap: Plan lists, operations and selectors may show data of other organizations, and new plans are created under a fixed organization.
gaps.impact: Confidentiality breach and wrong figures in multi-tenant use.
gaps.recommendation: Scope all plan data and creation to the user's organization.

gaps.gap: Decreases and transfers on parent levels ignore child allocations, and transfers within the same branch give non-intuitive results.
gaps.impact: Children can exceed their parent, distorting control.
gaps.recommendation: Validate against the unallocated balance or cascade to a chosen child; block same-branch transfers.

gaps.gap: Added levels are not recorded in the edit history and need no document.
gaps.impact: Structure changes to an approved plan are not traceable.
gaps.recommendation: Record every addition; confirm whether additions need a document.

gaps.gap: Participation changes apply immediately without document or history; inactive endowments may keep shares; per-level figures do not reconcile with the total share.
gaps.impact: Funding source allocation cannot be audited and reports may mislead endowment boards.
gaps.recommendation: Route participation changes through an evidenced, audited change and fix share calculations.

gaps.gap: Plan indicator achievement is a static value never updated from actual indicator results.
gaps.recommendation: Derive achievement from leaf indicators and accepted evidence, or define a manual update process.

gaps.gap: Levels cannot be deleted, moved or re-ordered.
gaps.recommendation: Confirm need; add evidenced delete/move with safeguards for linked records.

gaps.gap: Edit-session drafts are lost on refresh without warning; indicator changes in edit mode are saved immediately outside the session.
gaps.impact: Lost work and inconsistent change control.
gaps.recommendation: Warn before leaving, include indicator changes in the session or separate them clearly.

gaps.gap: Starting a new operation from the register with «all plans» selected silently targets the first plan.
gaps.impact: Operations may be executed on the wrong plan.
gaps.recommendation: Require explicit plan selection in the operation form.

gaps.gap: Operations are allowed on unapproved, inactive or locked plans.
gaps.impact: Budget changes on closed or draft plans.
gaps.recommendation: Define allowed operations per plan state and enforce them.

gaps.gap: Funding documents cannot be opened and fundings cannot be corrected or reversed.
gaps.impact: Errors in endowment size cannot be fixed with an audit trail.
gaps.recommendation: Allow opening documents and evidenced reversal entries.

gaps.gap: Two users adjusting the same plan at the same time can overwrite each other's changes.
gaps.recommendation: Apply changes as increments with locking at save time.

gaps.gap: Two different definitions of 'available' exist and diverge when payments exceed a project's budget.
gaps.recommendation: Use one definition everywhere and flag overpaid projects.

open_questions: Which roles may create plans, edit structure, approve plans, execute increases/decreases/transfers, lock/reopen plans and manage endowment funding and participation? Is maker ≠ approver required?
Is plan approval a formal multi-step workflow (e.g. CEO or board approval) rather than a status flag? Can an unapproved plan be used for linking or budget operations?
What exactly must happen to obligations marked «ترحَّل للخطة القادمة» when a plan is locked (automatic carry-over operations, re-linking projects, reporting only)?
Should decreases and transfers on parent levels be limited to the unallocated balance, or cascade to children? Are transfers within the same branch allowed?
May an organization have several plans for the same year, or several active plans at once?
Do additions of new levels to an approved plan require an official document and history?
Must users be able to delete, move or re-order levels, and what happens to linked projects, applications and indicators?
How is plan indicator achievement calculated and who maintains it?
Do endowment participation and split changes require an official document and approval, and where should splits be maintained?
Should a mismatch between children amounts and the parent amount block saving or approving a plan?
Which application statuses or review stages count as 'temporarily reserved' against a plan item?
Which budget operations are allowed on unapproved, inactive or locked plans?
How are erroneous endowment fundings corrected?
Must budget operations be approved (maker-checker) before being applied?
Should the AI document check ever block an operation, or remain advisory only?
What is the intended level taxonomy and maximum depth (track → item → initiative)?
Who is the audience of the endowment share report (e.g. endowment boards) and what format do they need?
